messages:
leila_fin: Quick heads-up 10K royalty invoice from Montreal Media (MM-ROY-2026). Vendor charged Canadian GST/HST and is asking Redwood to gross-up for a 15% Swiss withholding they say applies. Question: which countrys withholding/tax rules apply here? We're a US payer.

montreal_media: Hi Leila  sorry for confusion. We're Montreal Media SARL (Switzerland branch billing from CH bank). Invoice sent with CA GST because our Montreal office created the invoice. We believe Swiss law may require withholding on royalties paid to CH entity when paid from abroad. Requesting gross-up so we receive agreed net.

ian_tax: Few checks: 1) Determine payer entity (Redwood Inc vs Redwood EU/CA). 2) Source of royalty income and applicable treaty. US-Switzerland tax treaty may reduce/zero withholding on royalties if properly documented. 3) GST/HST is Canadian domestic tax and should only apply if supply taxed in Canada or vendor registered there.

matt_payments: AP: payment will be from Redwood Inc (US). We charged GL to US budget. So US-source rules govern.

leila_fin: So if Redwood Inc pays, we need either a valid W-8BEN-E from the vendor (or W-8BEN if individual) claiming treaty benefit and then we can withhold at treaty rate or 0%. We don't usually gross-up unless contract explicitly allows.

montreal_media: We can submit W-8BEN-E. We also want confirmation Redwood won't deduct unless required. If withholding occurs in Switzerland on receipt, they asked for gross-up.

ian_tax: Swiss inbound withholding on royalties is rare for corporate recipients with treaty relief. More likely: Switzerland doesn't tax most outbound royalties withheld at source. But we should not accept vendor's unilateral gross-up ask.

taxbot: :information_source: Automated rule: Missing W-8BEN-E -> default 30% withholding on certain US-source passive income. For royalties, backup withholding/trade treatment may apply.

matt_payments: AP will not pay until we receive completed W-8BEN-E and confirmation of billing country. Also need vendor to reissue invoice without Canadian GST if they are not registered in Canada for this supply.

ian_tax: Action items: 1) Ask vendor to upload W-8BEN-E and Swiss company registration (UID). 2) Ask vendor to reissue invoice: show payer Redwood Inc, remove CA GST if not applicable, and include bank details with country. 3) If vendor claims Swiss withholding, require statutory proof (tax receipt) before any gross-up discussion.

montreal_media: Got it. Uploading W-8BEN-E now (link: https://files.example/mm/w8bene-2026.pdf) and will reissue invoice. We'll defer gross-up claim until proof provided.

leila_fin: Thanks. AP will hold payment. Once W-8BEN-E validated and invoice corrected (no CA GST if not applicable), we'll process and apply withholding only if required by tax. No gross-ups without legal/contract approval.

matt_payments: :no_entry: Payment hold placed for MM-ROY-2026 pending docs.

ian_tax: I'll review the W-8BEN-E and reply with recommended withholding rate (treaty or statutory). If it's zero under US-CH treaty and docs are valid, we likely withhold 0%.

montreal_media: Thanks all, will reissue and send proof if any Swiss withholding actually happens after receipt. Apologies for messy invoice.
